stem.text: Find the interval of convergence of the power series \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{3 x^{n}}{3^{n} \sqrt{n}} \). Use the ratio test for the interior and justify the behaviour at each endpoint.

answer_key.label: The interval of convergence is \( -3 \le x < 3 \).

worked_solution.text: For the ratio test, form \( \left|\frac{\frac{3 x^{n+1}}{3^{n+1} \sqrt{n+1}}}{\frac{3 x^{n}}{3^{n} \sqrt{n}}}\right| \).
The series converges when \( \frac{\left|x\right|}{3} < 1 \), that is \( \left|x\right| < 3 \), so \( -3 < x < 3 \).

At \( x = 3 \) the series is \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{3}{\sqrt{n}} \), which diverges by the p-series test, since it is a multiple of a p-series with \( p = \frac{1}{2} \le 1 \). At \( x = -3 \) the series is \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{3 (-1)^n}{\sqrt{n}} \), which converges by the alternating series test, since its terms alternate and their sizes decrease to 0.
The interval of convergence is \( -3 \le x < 3 \).

options.label: The interval of convergence is \( -3 < x \le 3 \).
